location: docs/distillation_results.md:66-67; hf_readmes/README_sft-v1.md:93-94; hf_readmes/README_dpo-v1-scale.md:58,93; hf_readmes/README_distill-v1.md:123; hf_readmes/generate_cards.py:80,143,147; README.md:21
claim: UAR 70.0% and pra_lenient 15.30% are results of the DPO checkpoint (`dpo-v1-scale`), described as "SFT+DPO+memory".
actual: The tracked artifact results/v1_scale/E_sft_memory/metrics.json was produced by run_system_e_v1.py:35, which loads HFEngine("outputs/sft/v1/merged") — the SFT-only checkpoint, no DPO — and names the system E_sft_memory_v1 (line 95). docs/proper_scale_results.md:27 defines E as "SFT v1 + memory". No artifact in results/ measures any DPO checkpoint's pra_lenient or UAR; dpo-v1-scale appears only in the pairwise C-vs-E comparison.

claim: The distillation result is a +3.3pp pra_lenient gain (15.30% -> 18.59%) attributed to on-policy distillation.
actual: The two rows compare different training lineages: E = outputs/sft/v1/merged (SFT only) and E-distill = outputs/distill/v1/merged, which configs/training/distill_v1.yaml and README.md:99-100 describe as chaining off the DPO output. The +3.3pp therefore spans both the DPO stage and the distillation stage. The distillation-specific measurement is the pairwise C-vs-F run (C = DPO+memory, F = distill+memory), results/v1_scale/C_vs_F_distill_pairwise/summary.json: f_wins 40 (38.1%) vs c_wins 32 (30.5%), +7.6pp.

claim: PMB is "688 adversarial probes across 40 personas".
actual: data/benchmarks/pmb_v0_full/probes.jsonl contains 8 distinct persona_id values (p000-p007), 86 probes each. data/benchmarks/pmb_v0_full/DATASHEET.md states "Personas: 8". 40 is the count of SFT *training* personas in data/benchmarks/sft_personas_v1/, and 40 is also the facts-per-persona value. The same README correctly says "8 categories" on line 24.

claim: Base model revision is pinned by commit SHA, not a moving tag (`base_model_revision` in each config).
actual: Only configs/training/sft.yaml and sft_v1.yaml pin a SHA (3e22461f...). configs/training/dpo.yaml, dpo_v1_scale.yaml, dpo_v1_more_epochs.yaml and distill_v1.yaml all set base_model_revision: "main"; distill_v1.yaml also sets teacher_model_revision: "main". Reproducibility is therefore claimed for runs that are not revision-pinned.

location: README.md:175-177; hf_readmes/gguf_README.md files table vs its own evaluation table; docs/quantization_results.md:51-53
claim: GGUF file sizes F16 8.64 GiB / Q8_0 4.61 GiB / Q4_K_M 3.18 GiB.
actual: The same documents also state 8.62 / 4.59 / 3.17 GiB. hf_readmes/gguf_README.md contains both sets in one file (Files table vs Evaluation table). docs/quantization_results.md:18 states the F16 file as "9.27GB" (= 8.63 GiB) while its own table says 8.62 GiB. No llama-bench output or GGUF file is committed (*.gguf is gitignored), so neither set is re-derivable from a tracked artifact.

claim: Quantization figures: llama-bench throughput (585.07/492.33/633.00 pp512, 26.15/43.07/58.00 tg128), imatrix 5328 chunks at n_ctx=512 with PPL 2.7258 +/- 0.0046, "model reports as 4.63B params", and every per-file GGUF size.
actual: git ls-files shows no quantization or benchmark artifact is tracked; .gitignore excludes *.gguf and results/ contains no quantization output. Every figure is restated from run logs that are not in the repository. The only other restatement is hardcoded literals in scripts/generate_linkedin_figures.py (untracked), so it is not independent corroboration.

claim: GGUF quantization preserves generation quality — "Confirmed down to Q4_K_M by manual + automated checks".
actual: docs/quantization_results.md verifies coherent, in-character output at Q3_K_S and Q3_K_M as well, and states "Q3_K_S is the smallest verified-coherent level, for both" checkpoints. The README understates its own result. The checks described are manual llama-cli / llama-mtmd-cli runs; no automated quality check is evidenced.

claim: Importance-matrix (imatrix) quantization "used no imatrix calibration data — a real next step".
actual: Contradicted by docs/quantization_results.md:119-143 of the same repository, which documents the imatrix calibration corpus, a llama-imatrix run, and 6 levels requantized with --imatrix and uploaded to a private repo. The stale bullet had no date stamp. What genuinely remains open is the imatrix-vs-non-imatrix generation-quality comparison, which was never finished.

claim: title "onebee-gf: Stretching a 1B Parameter LLM...", version 0.0.0, author "Arrochi", url github.com/arrogance231/onebee-gf.
actual: pyproject.toml:7 sets version 0.1.0. README.md:3 describes the model as ~2B effective-parameter and docs/quantization_results.md:45 reports 4.63B params — not 1B. The repository is github.com/arjhinety/small-mind-companion; there is no repo at the cited URL and README.md:154 documents the rename. The author string matched neither README.md's BibTeX ("arrogance231") nor the HF owner (arrochi112).

claim: Model-card front matter `license: gemma` and "Inherits Gemma's license terms from the base model".
actual: All seven generated/pushed cards declare `license: apache-2.0` and "Apache-2.0, inherited from the base model"; CITATION.cff and README.md:222 also say Apache-2.0. The template contradicted every artifact it produced. The underlying claim that Apache-2.0 is inherited from google/gemma-4-E2B-it is not verifiable from this repository.

location: README.md:78 (pre-fix) vs data/distill/v1/DATASHEET.md:9-11 vs docs/proper_scale_results.md:10, docs/day4_sft_v1_results.md:21, docs/dpo_results.md:123
claim: Contamination-check status of the SFT v1 corpus, stated in both directions at once: "not yet checked" in the SFT datasheets, "already contamination-checked clean" in the distill datasheet — which cites data/sft/v1/DATASHEET.md, a file that said the opposite.
actual: The check was actually run during this audit: `python scripts/check_contamination.py --train-glob "data/sft/v1/train.jsonl" --eval-glob "data/benchmarks/pmb_v0_full/probes.jsonl"` -> "No contamination found." (exit 0). Same result for data/sft/v0/train.jsonl. The data is clean; the "not yet checked" datasheet text was stale, and the distill datasheet was citing a file that disagreed with it.

claim: Persona corpora generated with "seed 9999" (v0) and "seed 31415" (v1).
actual: Neither number appears anywhere in the repository. The persona corpora were generated by scripts/build_pmb.py, whose --seed default is 1337; generate_sft_data.py uses random.Random(4242). As documented, persona generation is not reproducible.

claim: The DPO preference pairs were built with "the same pipeline as data/sft/v1".
actual: Measured against the current data/sft/v1/train.jsonl: 2263/2277 user turns match but 0/2277 system texts match. Both datasets call ContextBuilder.build(..., recent_turns[-6:]), so identical inputs would produce identical system text. Git timestamps show the DPO set was generated before SFT v1's dedup fix and ratio rebalance, so the retrieval contexts diverged. The cause was not pinned down. "Same pipeline" holds as generator code, not as prompt construction.

claim: "451 passing" tests (badge and project-structure block) and "21 real environment/API/tooling bugs".
actual: tests/** contains 473 `def test_` functions, and docs/research_questions.md:185 states "473 total passing". docs/model_quirks.md numbers its entries 1 through 27. Both README figures were stale.

claim: "All training and quantization runs were done on a single rented workstation GPU (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell class, ~96GB VRAM)".
actual: docs/quantization_results.md:11-16 states the quantization box had no system-wide CUDA toolkit (nvcc) and that llama.cpp was built CPU-only, that conversion/quantization are CPU-only tools regardless, and that the source checkpoint was downloaded because "the previous GPU box was deleted". docs/quantization_results.md:160-161 records the distill-v1 GGUF build as running on Modal (RTX-PRO-6000).

claim: "## Regenerate figures: make figures", presented as part of the chain where "Every command above should be run from a clean clone, in order, to earn the reproducibility claim."
actual: scripts/make_figures.py does not exist, so the target always fails. The `paper` target likewise references paper/build.sh, which does not exist (paper/ holds only .gitkeep placeholders). A reproducibility chain that includes a command which cannot run does not earn the claim.

claim: "Full quantization spread (F16 through Q2_K, 12 levels)".
actual: F16 plus 12 quantized levels is 13 GGUF text files; with the vision projector the release is 14 files. "12 levels" counts only the llama-quantize outputs while the stated range F16->Q2_K implies 13.

location: hf_readmes/README_distill-v1-gguf.md files table vs its own header and hf_readmes/README_dpo-v1-scale-gguf.md
claim: Q3_K_M is the "recommended smallest safe level".
actual: The same card's files table marks the smaller Q3_K_S as "Verified coherent, in-character", and docs/quantization_results.md:186 names Q3_K_S as the smallest verified-coherent level for both checkpoints. The header of the same card says "Use Q3_K_S or above".

claim: All titled "# PMB v0 - Personalised Memory Benchmark" with the PMB overview text.
actual: Only data/benchmarks/pmb_v0_full/ is the PMB evaluation benchmark. sft_personas_v0 (4 personas / 344 probes) and sft_personas_v1 (40 personas / 3437 probes) are training-persona corpora, and pmb_v0 (2 personas / 36 probes) is a fixture-scale smoke test. Root cause: scripts/build_pmb.py:761 hardcoded the PMB title regardless of --out-dir.

claim: "This run (8 personas) may not be the full v0 benchmark (target: 8 personas)."
actual: Self-contradictory: it reports 8 personas and names 8 as the target. scripts/build_pmb.py was fixed in commit 78cf358 to suppress this line when n_personas >= 8, but the corpus was committed 65 seconds later (a170dc8) still carrying it.

claim: "Every dataset directory has a hash.txt and DATASHEET.md".
actual: data/distill/v1/ has a DATASHEET.md but no hash.txt, which was never committed. The directory's contents are therefore not integrity-pinned, and it carries no hash file while every other dataset directory does.

claim: PMB probes ship with "a gold answer, supporting-memory IDs, and acceptable alternatives".
actual: The acceptable_alternatives field is present on all 688 probes and is empty in 688/688. Exact-match pra_strict is consequently ~0 in every run (0.0-0.49%), which is why pra_lenient is the reported metric. The field is documented as a capability that is not populated.

claim: `make lint` / `make typecheck` work after the documented `uv sync`.
actual: ruff, black, mypy and pytest are declared only in the `dev` extra of pyproject.toml; the base `uv sync` does not install them, so these targets fail on a clean clone. .github/workflows/ci.yml uses the same bare `uv sync` pattern.

claim: Link to "README's Engineering highlights" at README.md#engineering-highlights.
actual: README.md contains no such heading; the section was rewritten to "Results & Analysis" in commit de16547. The anchor is dead.

claim: `dpo-v1-scale` is the "current best checkpoint overall".
actual: `distill-v1` superseded it (README.md:150, hf_readmes/README_distill-v1.md:19, docs/quantization_results.md:158). The template, the card generator and the quantization doc header all still named the DPO checkpoint as current-best, contradicting the same files' later sections.

claim: "...check results/imatrix_perplexity_comparison.md if it exists for the outcome".
actual: The file does not exist anywhere in the repository, and no equivalent artifact was committed. Confirmed absent by directory listing and content search. The imatrix quality claim therefore rests on a perplexity estimate and a qualitative check only.

claim: The imatrix calibration corpus is "~11MB / 15k lines".
actual: data/imatrix_calibration.txt is 11,086,366 bytes (11 MB, correct) but 66,383 lines — roughly 4.4x the stated count.

claim: The document's headline results table, linked from README.md as "current authoritative results".
actual: The table reports the first v1_scale run, produced before the dedup fix and with a detector that did not recognise the model's correct abstention phrasing. Its UAR values (31.25%, 16.25%) are superseded by 25.0% and 70.0% later in the same document (line 182). The document disclosed this in a limitations bullet at line 217 but the README's "current authoritative" label did not.

claim: "Every dataset directory has a hash.txt" and, in the audit's first pass, "all six hash.txt files match once CRLF is normalised to LF".
actual: The six split in two. The four SFT/DPO hashes (data/sft/v0, data/sft/v1, data/dpo/v0, data/dpo/v1_scale) DO match, under sha256 over concatenated LF-normalised sorted *.jsonl. The four benchmark hashes do NOT match under any of thirteen tested algorithms: path as str() vs as_posix(); data as raw bytes, text, or LF-normalised; sha256 over path+data, data-only, or probes.jsonl-only; walk order vs name order; DATASHEET.md included or excluded. The mismatch is present on a clean git worktree of ae75ca9, the commit that introduced the files, so it is not caused by the audit's edits. Cause undetermined. The first-pass sentence generalised from the four that passed to all six.

claim: The SFT v1 dataset is 2242 examples (2017 train / 225 val).
actual: The committed data/sft/v1/ is 2480 examples (2232 train / 248 val). 2242 was the FIRST v1 generation; it was regenerated twice the same day (dedup fix, then ratio rebalance) and the count changed each time. docs/sft/v1/DATASHEET.md and README.md had the correct 2232/248; three result docs still quoted the superseded number as current.

claim: System D (raw + retrieval memory) scores 15.10% pra_lenient, a +14.9pp / +2.7pp gain over the no-memory baseline.
actual: results/v0.1/D_memory/metrics.json holds pra_lenient = 0.1513157894736842 (92/608), which is 15.13%, not 15.10%. Six documents quoted the wrong rounding, and two derived deltas repeated it (+14.9pp and +2.7pp; correct: +15.0pp and +2.6pp). Missed by the first audit pass, which checked that the documents agreed with each other rather than that they matched the artifact; found by the claims-matrix validator, which recomputes the value.

claim: Every dataset directory carries a hash.txt, and the integrity-pinning story covers the committed corpora.
actual: Two committed probe sets -- data/benchmarks/h22_judgment (H22 abliteration judgment quality, 24 probes) and data/benchmarks/emotional_range (H24, 10 registers) -- appeared in neither scripts/recompute_hashes.py nor scripts/validate.py, so neither had a hash.txt and neither was covered by the freeze or any integrity check. Found by validate.py hygiene check unpinned-probe-sets, not by reading. The corpus count is 11, not the nine every document claimed.

claim: The validator, the result registry it checks, and the CI gate that runs them, pass.
actual: They passed on Windows and failed in CI. Three checks compared raw bytes: sha256 over un-normalised file bytes in result_registry_hashes_match and build_result_registry.sha256_file, and path.stat().st_size == 11086366 for the imatrix calibration corpus. This repo has no .gitattributes and sets core.autocrlf=true, so the Windows working tree is CRLF (11086366 bytes; 81998 more than the LF form) while GitHub Actions checks out LF. Four tests failed in CI while 510 passed locally: registry-results-index-fresh, registry-result-registry-metrics, datasheet-imatrix-calibration-not-11mb-15k, and the two that aggregate them.
